citation.title: Equivariant neural operators for gradient-consistent topology optimization
citation.venue: Journal of Computational Design and Engineering 11(3), 91-100

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The tested neural solvers reduce full SIMP inference runtime by about fourfold or more relative to the paper's finite-difference solver.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 5.3 states at least a fourfold improvement. Table 2 reports 75 s classical and 19 s for the equivariant U-Net FNO, a derived 75/19 = 3.95-fold speed-up for the proposed model; fourfold is rounded.
claim.alternatives: Section 5.3 says a single FDM solve on 160,000 voxels takes almost 5 min versus less than 1 s for a neural operator; Table 2 lists 75 s classical versus 2-19 s across neural models.

baseline.implementation: DL4TO software library used for experiments (Section 5.1); exact classical solver implementation not stated
baseline.solver: FDM spatial discretization stated; linear-system solver not stated (Sections 5.2 and Table 2)
baseline.hardware_ml: Intel Xeon Silver 4210 CPU for inference (Table 2); GeForce RTX 2080 Ti GPU for training (Section 5.1)
baseline.problem_size: 39 x 39 x 4 voxel test grid (Section 5.1); an additional 160,000-voxel PDE-solve example appears in Section 5.3
baseline.classical_time: 75 s average complete SIMP run on Intel Xeon Silver 4210 CPU (Table 2)
baseline.ml_time: 19 s average complete SIMP run with proposed equivariant U-Net FNO on same CPU (Table 2)
baseline.training_time: 2-14 h across models and dataset sizes (Section 5.1)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; Section 5.1 says training trajectories came from 60 SIMP iterations on each of 10-200 problems
baseline.quality_metric: IoU, failed-design percentage, FE-related mean compliance, trajectory WMAE (Section 5.2, Table 1)
baseline.quality_gap: For equivariant U-Net FNO trained on 200 trajectories, Table 1 reports IoU 0.73, fail rate 6.25%, compliance 0.56; baseline values are not tabulated there

R1.evidence: Tables 1-2: runtime is measured for fixed 60-iteration runs, while learned designs differ from classical outputs (IoU 0.73 and 6.25% failed for the proposed model trained on 200 trajectories); no equal-quality or equal-time comparison is given.

R2.evidence: Table 2 times both methods on Intel Xeon Silver 4210 CPU. The text does not establish R2(a)-(e), and does not state the FDM linear solver.

R3.evidence: Section 5.1 gives 2-14 h training times and says each training trajectory used 60 SIMP iterations, but does not give data-generation wall-clock cost or a break-even use count.

R4.evidence: Section 5.2 and Table 1 report returned-design compliance and stress/connectivity failure rates, but no volume-fraction or equivalent constraint-satisfaction results are reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: not stated; Section 5.1 describes a dataset of almost 10,000 problems and 10-200 training trajectories, without the test split count

notes: The abstract asserts speed-ups without a number, and Section 5.3 supplies the first quantitative classical comparison. The paper reports quality against ground-truth SIMP and a design failure definition, but the classical quality values are not paired with the timing comparison. Public experiment code is not stated in the article.
